pages.titre: How to reach us, about a figure or an engagement.
pages.lede: Name the figure you are questioning and where you saw it. Every number here has a source, so we start from the same one. No attachments.
pages.description: A first message that names a figure and its source starts a real discussion. Attach no file: this tool exists so your documents stay with you.

sections.h2: Two ways to reach us, email and a public issue
html: Write to contact@cascade-routing.com: the direct channel. For anything worth deciding in the open (a disputed figure, a wrong line, a question others will have), open an issue at github.com/ArslaneSempai-ui/cascade-routing. An issue is public, so keep confidential material out of it: no client names, no records, no internal figures. Either way, attach no file: a channel for records is opened in the engagement letter, before signature, like every other term.

The page you are on and the figure you dispute: each one here has a declared source, so we can meet at it. If you disagree with a measurement, bring your own rerun. The record is frozen and the command is public, so you can reproduce it. If you measured your own cases, bring the report the tool wrote beside your CSV: it contains rates and their confidence intervals, and no values from your documents.

We receive none of your records. We do not want a sample either. The tool exists so your documents never leave your machine. A sample attached to a public issue is published, and a clone, once made, cannot be taken back. If your question needs your data, the answer is a command that runs where the data lives, and we will point you to it.

Two shortcuts. On a fresh clone, node src/premiere-reponse.mjs prints the conclusion in under a second, with what would flip it. And the eight objections a bank's reviewers actually raise are already answered, mechanism by mechanism, in Appendix C, Questions below.

pages.titre: Not in the record. Nothing lives at this address.
pages.lede: This page was never measured, never sealed, never published: the address is wrong, or the page has moved. Everything that exists is one link away: the findings on the main screen, and the six appendices in the footer below.

This page says who publishes the site, under which licences, where it is served from, and whether it sets cookies or tracks visitors. It follows the same rule as the rest of the site, so each figure on it has a stated source.
pages.description: Who publishes this site, under which licences, where it is served from, and whether it sets cookies or tracks visitors (it does neither).

html: This site, and the tool it describes, are published by Arslane Chaouche. He is the licensor named in the first line of the licence file that ships with the tool.

The tool is licensed PolyForm Noncommercial, with a thirty‑day Evaluation Grant, a right to evaluate the tool that is written into the licence file. The full terms are in Appendix D. The text and figures of this site are by the same author. The typeface is Literata, by TypeTogether, under the SIL Open Font Licence, and it is served from this site's own files. The objects pictured on the appendix pages were modelled for this site by its author.
The site is static files, which GitHub Pages serves straight from the public repository that holds them. No server code of ours runs to show you this page.

sections.h2: What this site does to visitors: nothing
html: No cookies, no analytics, no tracking, no forms. The scripts on this site do two things only. The main screen keeps its animation and the browser tab title in step with each other. The appendix pages open their sections when you print. You can switch the scripts off and the site still works. Each number shown here has a stated source, and the file that states each source is public, next to this page: releve.json. Those numbers come from our public test set, a file we froze. A content hash is a code that identifies a file by its contents. The one in the masthead, the band at the top of the page, is the content hash of that frozen file.

The tool publishes a retraction file, which lists each published conclusion that turned out to be wrong, and a test holds that file open. The same applies to this site. When a number here is corrected, the correction is made in the open and the change is recorded.
